sitrep.mission: The ruling door for V-1…V-8 and the firewall touch
sitrep.gate_purpose: Rule the eight items that four vaults (Terminal · City · LatticeProtocol · Automator) plus Socials and Home are waiting on; name the firewall touch LIP-0011 will make; grant or refuse the push / memo-delivery / receiver GOs.

composite_title: Vernier P1 exit — one field, four waiters, eight rulings
composite_question: Operation Vernier found at P1 that sync.sync_hash has a validated shape and no defined semantic. In the 25 days the gate waited, four vaults asked the same question independently and one of them (LatticeProtocol) carded its generator on our answer. Sections V-1…V-3 are the original findings re-derived on the live subject (Terminal.aDNA, 8 canvases); V-4…V-8 are the inbox's additions; the last section names the firewall touch and the GOs. Each section leads with the measurement and prices the migration; ruling ‘defer’ or choosing a non-recommended option is a real answer and is recorded as one.

sections.title: V-1 · What does sync.sync_hash hash? — three readings pass today, and four vaults are waiting
sections.question: canvas_std.compute_sync_hash hashes topology (sorted node ids + edge pairs, 16 hex). Terminal's 8 canvases store sha256(source markdown)[:16] (re-derived today: 8/8 source match · 0/8 topology match). City's twin stores the topology hash plus a non-standard sync.source_sha256. LatticeProtocol ADR-018 + LinkML Profile v0.1 define it as the master file's bytes, and gen-canvas (M-B1) is carded on your answer. Rule A-6 checks 16 hex chars only; the spec never says what is hashed. Which option? (a) sync_hash = source/master bytes · (b) sync_hash stays topology and the Standard registers sync.source_sha256 (64 hex) · (c) split into sync.topology_hash + sync.source_hash with sync_hash a deprecated alias through v2.x.
sections.rec_label: (b) — additive; every canvas that passes today keeps passing; Terminal and LP migrate one key; City already does it
sections.analysis:
• Migration priced per option. (a) breaks compute_sync_hash, Canvas's 26 adna_native canvases, City's topology usage, and every round-trip loader; requires a major bump. (b) breaks nothing that passes; Terminal moves its source hash from sync_hash to source_sha256 and regenerates (their generator already computes it); LP's gen-canvas writes both from day one; Home's one canvas is already non-conformant on other grounds. (c) is (b) with a rename nobody asked for and an alias to maintain.
  • Why topology stays in sync_hash. §8.1 already calls it 'the sync hash of the authoritative-source topology'; A-6 is in the round-trip layer because the hash↔source check is the round-trip's job. Noether's own argument for (a) — 'a schema master has no fromNode→toNode topology' — is an argument that the twin has one and the master needs a different key, i.e. for Q2.
  • What A-6 gains. With (b): source_sha256 must be 64 hex when present; when production: generated the validator may recompute topology and compare (ruled in P2b as advisory or hard — recommend advisory at extended, hard at adna_native).
  • Vernier P1's own observation stands: a source hash is the more useful question for a view canvas ('has my source moved?') and is third-party verifiable — (b) keeps it, named.
  • ⛔ Not a signature on the Standard. This verdict instructs LIP-0011 (P2b); the firewall touch is named in the Firewall section below and signed with the LIP.
  • ⛩ Replies since this door was rendered (added 2026-10-13, receipt db21711, byte-unchanged). LatticeProtocol (Noether): "no objection to (b); LP withdraws (a)", and its two one-line amends (ADR-018 point 6 · the LinkML profile description, routed to Pāṇini) land at M-B1, after the verdict, not before. Terminal (Vauban): (b) "accepted in direction"; they migrate once, after the P4 verdict, not on the interim. City: already writes and checks sync.source_sha256 (measured 10-12, no new reply). Automator (Berthier): no reply yet. ⇒ 3 of the 4 asking vaults are aligned on (b) by their own written statements (LP · Terminal in prose; City in code). The fourth has not spoken. ⛔ Their positions are evidence, not a verdict. All three state that they wait on this door's .output.json.

recommendation.rationale: Choose (b). It is the only option with zero breakage for every current passer, it is what City already does, and it answers Noether Q1 '(b)' and Q2 'yes' in one stroke.
key_factors: Terminal + LP migrate one key each; City migrates none
A-6 gains a semantic check it never had
risks: Terminal's 8 canvases read 'stale' to a conformant loader until they regenerate (they already do so daily)
(a) partisans — LP ADR-018 — must amend one line; memo #22 says so plainly
next_actions: P2b drafts LIP-0011 from this verdict
Memo #22/#21/#23 carry the verdict, not the recommendation
Fleet backward-compat census run before the LIP is signed

sections.title: V-2 · A-8 is gated behind aDNA-Native — a correct axis pair is inert at extended
sections.question: All 8 Terminal canvases declare extended, carry the correct authority: view + production: generated, and nothing validates the pair at that tier; an invented value would pass. They would validate adna_native today by flipping one field (8/8, re-derived). Should A-8 run at extended too?
sections.rec_label: Yes, at extended — but measure the fleet count of extended canvases carrying a bad value FIRST (P2b), and ship it as validate-if-present
sections.analysis:
• The axes answer who owns the meaning · how is it made — a question about any derived canvas, not an aDNA-Native one. The keys sit in the native tier for reasons that predate the axes (LIP-0010 placed them where the other _reserved checks were).
  • Price: any extended canvas with an invalid axis value starts failing. Unknown count today — P2b measures before the LIP is signed; if it is >0 the LIP prices the migration per vault.
  • Both keys stay optional; only their values are validated when present (LIP-0010's asymmetric rule unchanged).

recommendation.rationale: Rule 'yes, pending the measured count'. A tier that lets a correct pair go unchecked is the F-DT-7 shape — an instrument failing into reassurance.
key_factors: Validate-if-present cannot break a canvas that omits the keys
risks: Fleet count unknown until P2b runs it
next_actions: P2b: census of extended canvases × axis values
LIP-0011 carries the tier change if count permits

sections.title: V-3 · generator as a provenance key — Terminal invented it (8/8), Home used it as an authority value
sections.question: Terminal carries _reserved.generator: what/canvas/build_canvases.py on all 8 (legal per §7.3, undeclared). Home's what/canvas/topology.canvas carries authority: "generator" at the non-canonical metadata._reserved with no production (confirmed today). LIP-0010 struck generator from the authority axis for conflating who owns the meaning with how it is made; Terminal reinvented it as the distinction LIP-0010 was drawing. Adopt a provenance carrier — and where?
sections.rec_label: Adopt as sync.generator (path or URN), not a top-level key — Terminal migrates by moving one key; authority: "generator" stays invalid
sections.analysis:
• sync is already the provenance block (source_name, source_version); how it was made belongs beside what it was made from.
  • A top-level _reserved.generator would be the 12th reserved key for one field; inside sync it is a property of an existing object — smaller schema change, same information.
  • Home's canvas is non-conformant on three counts (path · authority value · missing production) and is Hestia's to fix; V-6 rules whether a grandfathering note exists for it. Reported, not repaired here.
  • ⛩ Reply since rendering (2026-10-13). Terminal accepts generator → sync.generator "in the same regeneration" as V-1. That is one regeneration in total, run after P4.

recommendation.rationale: Register sync.generator in LIP-0011; decline a top-level key; decline reinstating generator as an authority value.
next_actions: Memo #21 to Terminal names the move

sections.title: V-4 · Boulogne B14 — the dual-mode schema pack (LinkML master + canvas twin + image + prose, one sync hash)
sections.question: Automator (Berthier) asks the Standard to state: canonical direction (master → twin via ACADÉMIE P3 gen-canvas), the round-trip invariant, a loss table, twin authoring rules ('none, if production: generated'), and loading modes text / diagram / both in spec_canvas_context_loading. City asks where the rule lives (recommends: Canvas Standard, ADR-062 cross-refers) and offers its pack as a derivability fixture. Default if silent: Boulogne drafts it proposed in its own vault naming Canvas 'as counterparty, not as consenting'. Accept, amend, or decline as a T2 item?
sections.rec_label: Accept as a T2 item: a pack profile in the Standard (semantic_bindings.profile) + loading modes in spec_canvas_context_loading; ADR-062 owns the LinkML side
sections.analysis:
• The pack is pattern_diagrammatic_context with a schema master instead of prose — the dual-channel row the axes were built for. Declining it would push a Canvas-shaped rule into a vault that does not validate canvases.
  • Loading modes are a canvas_context loader concern (leg 2); text/diagram/both is a three-line extension with a scoring fixture City has offered to supply.
  • What Canvas does not take: the LinkML master's own rules, gen-canvas's implementation, the image render (Design's). The pack's invariant — 'no member lands alone' — is a release-train rule and stays Boulogne's.

recommendation.rationale: Accept; the Standard gains a pack profile and a loading-modes section; City's pack becomes a certification fixture in P2b/P4.
key_factors: Three vaults asked for the same home
It is diagrammatic context by another master
risks: Pack profile text must not describe LinkML — stay substrate-neutral
next_actions: P4 writes the profile + loading modes
Memo #24 to Automator accepts as T2

sections.title: V-5 · Boulogne B18 — every graph carries what/canvas/graph.canvas, plus a live overlay
sections.question: B18: each graph carries a generated graph.canvas (view/generated, sync = hash of structural inputs, regenerated by a STATE hook, a hand-edit is a validator FAIL) with a volatile live overlay (sessions, lease mode, commit age, open gates, locks). Rule: overlay as a group inside graph.canvas, or a second file (graph_activity.canvas)? City (third viewer) asks to read graph.canvas as a building's floorplan and the overlay as live state joined by node id.
sections.rec_label: Second file keyed by the base canvas's node ids, never merged (Berthier's default; City concurs) — and Canvas builds its own graph.canvas first (P5)
sections.analysis:
• A volatile overlay inside a generated canvas makes every heartbeat a regeneration and every regeneration a sync-hash change — the base would never be 'fresh'. Two files, two cadences.
  • The overlay's _reserved.sync names the base hash it was drawn against, so a stale overlay is detectable with the V-1 machinery.
  • City's floorplan reading is a read of a conformant canvas — nothing to rule beyond 'yes'; layout positions (Λ) stay City-private as they self-ruled.
  • The standard-bearer eats the law first: P5 builds Canvas's own graph.canvas with skill_canvas_producer_build before P4 writes the rule for others.

recommendation.rationale: Second file; profile graph for the base, overlay keyed by node id; floorplan reading yes; Λ stays City's.
risks: A STATE hook regenerating canvases is Boulogne's to build, not ours

sections.title: V-6 · _reserved placement for generated canvases — spec as written, or a grandfathering note?
sections.question: The spec says _reserved MUST live at metadata.frontmatter._reserved (ADR-011: 194 fleet canvases still have it at metadata._reserved). Home's topology.canvas is one of them. Automator asks: spec as written, or a grandfathering note? Default if silent: spec as written, Home's finding → Hestia as a conformance question.
sections.rec_label: Spec as written. Grandfathering is a migration note (ADR-011's partition already covers it), not a rule — Home's finding goes to Hestia
sections.analysis:
• A block at the wrong path 'carries semantics no tool reads while reporting green at core' (F-B1-1) — grandfathering it would license exactly that.
  • ADR-011 (pending your signature at its own door) already rules the legacy population and its two-population migration; a second rule here would be a second registry.
  • Generated canvases have no excuse: the generator writes the path once.

recommendation.rationale: Spec as written; one migration note in P4 pointing at ADR-011; Home's canvas memo'd to Hestia with the three counts named.
risks: ADR-011 is itself unsigned — sign it at its door

sections.title: V-7 · Noether's lattice dispositions + four CEL rewrites — OVERDUE (due before ACADÉMIE P3; P3 opened 2026-10-10)
sections.question: LP proposes: lattice_{comic,presentation}_canvas.lattice.yaml + example_canvas_v2.lattice.yaml = not-a-lattice, moving to 'the Canvas format' (ADR-008(3)/016(1)); 16 elsewhere-owned canvasforge files (SuperLeague ×13, SS ×3) = not-a-lattice landing in our format (ADR-010) — does the Canvas format receive them, and does it have a home (suffix, schema)? Plus four CEL rewrites (AND→&&, OR→||, iteration_count→iteration) in those two files. Measured: our two files are consumed by one federation test, one archived smoke test, and a pointer in AILedger Folio's dossier — no runtime executes them.
sections.rec_label: Confirm not-a-lattice for our three; apply the four CEL rewrites anyway (documents should compile); DECLINE to receive the 16 — the Standard describes canvases, not the pipelines that make them, and has no home for workflow descriptions
sections.analysis:
• Our two files are documentation of producer pipelines (comic · presentation). Keeping them readable as valid lattices costs four token edits and keeps the federation test honest; calling them runnable would be false.
  • 'The Canvas format' means .canvas — a 2-D output primitive. A workflow description is not one. Receiving the 16 would invent a format to hold them; the honest answer is 'no home here; they stay lattice-documentation in their owning vaults or archive'.
  • AILedger Folio points at lattice_presentation_canvas.lattice.yaml by path — any rename is memo'd to Thoth first (P5).
  • Overdue: memo #22 goes today with this recommendation marked provisional; the verdict follows from this door.

recommendation.rationale: Confirm rows 1–2 as not-a-lattice (documentation-only); decline row 3's 'landing in your format'; answer the home question 'none, by design'; accept all four CEL rewrites.
risks: LP's P7 migration may want a disposition for the 16 — SuperLeague/SS own them

sections.title: V-8 · Socials — social formats today? style_ref? read-only RLHF rows? is iii_quality_contract.md binding?
sections.question: Stentor asked twice (09-21, 10-06). Measured: post_generator has advisory char budgets + aspect hints (twitter/x 16:9 · linkedin 1.91:1 · instagram 1:1), no pixel envelopes, carousel, quote card or thumbnail, no style_ref. Socials' SG-4 blocks on answer (1); they say 'a not-yet is an answer'. (2) style_ref {taste_ref, kept_refs, constraints} by reference on Post/PostPanel. (3) read-only access to ADR-005 RLHF rows for variant ids they requested. (4) pin iii_quality_contract.md as the consumption contract. (5, added 2026-10-13) Should the Socials direct image bridge close before the verdict memo, or on it (default)?
sections.rec_label: (1) 'Not yet' + charter P7 to build it · (2) accept as a producer-model change · (3) yes to Canvas-side capture sidecars under their namespace, III store is Argus's · (4) yes, versioned
sections.analysis:
• None of this touches the Standard — it is producer-level, Canvas's to answer without a LIP. Only the priority is yours: P7 is a real build (~160k tokens).
  • 'Not yet' unblocks SG-4 today: their routing duty gets a named counterparty and a chartered mission instead of a silence.
  • spec_rlhf_seam.md: Canvas owns capture, III owns the store schema (§6b). Read-only to our sidecars under rlhf_consumer_namespace.socials.* is ours to grant; the III store is not.
  • C2PA/IPTC at generation time (their implicit flag): Canvas emits prompts, not pixels, in post_generator — the metadata belongs where pixels are written (Socials' encode step or ComfyUI's emitter). Say so.
  • ⛩ Reply since rendering (2026-10-13), carried verbatim at Stentor's request: "no Socials date forces P7 earlier than LIP-0011." SG-4 fired 10-07 and SG-5 fired 10-12; their P5 is text-only on the Canvas seam. Their counterparty_confirmed flag stays false until the P4 memo cites this door's .output.json. Disclosed: at SG-5 their operator ruled a bounded direct Qwen-Image bridge (Fal + Replicate, keys via the Home broker). It closes when our verdict memo arrives. Nothing it produces is a Canvas artifact, and it never touches the Standard. They ask: "if your verdict wants the bridge closed earlier, say so." The default is to let it close on the verdict memo. Closing it earlier would leave them with no image lane until P7.

recommendation.rationale: Answer all four now (memo #25); charter P7; sequence P7 after P2b unless SG-4's date forces it earlier.
key_factors: Unblocks a peer gate with an honest answer
risks: P7 competes with P2b for the next sitting

sections.title: Firewall touch #7 and the three GOs this session owes you
sections.question: Firewall: P2b will touch canvas_std/reserved.py (A-6 semantic · A-8 tier), roundtrip.py (source digest helper), schema/adna_canvas_v2.schema.json ($defs.reserved.sync), spec_adna_canvas_standard.md §7.2/§8.1, __init__.py (2.5.0) — named here so the LIP's signature is informed; the touch itself is signed with LIP-0011. GOs: ① push (2 pre-session commits + this session's; gitleaks pre-push); ② deliver the substantive replies after this door's verdicts (interim acks went today on the plan's approval); ③ standing permission to restart the Canvas-rooted gate_receiver when found down (it was down today; restarted; landed on :8767; four doors re-rendered). Also pointed at, not re-rendered: the four 26-day-old doors (adr_010 · adr_011 · adr_012 · operator_queue_20260916) — sign, or abandon per Home ADR-017.
sections.rec_label: Grant ① ② ③; sign adr_010 + adr_012 + queue ①③⑤ now; hold adr_011 with queue ② (memo #20) as before
sections.analysis:
• Push: authorship uniform (Mondrian), gitleaks clean history, visibility public — nothing in this session's changeset is a secret; the memos redacted infrastructure literals per the inbox README.
  • Receiver: a persistent local service — the 09-16 ruling started it once; a standing permission turns the next outage into a one-line act instead of a held gate.
  • The four old doors are unchanged in content; only their receiver URL moved. Their recommended order from 09-16 stands.

recommendation.rationale: Grant the three GOs; the firewall acknowledgement here is informational — the signature comes with LIP-0011.
